data.content_ref: inline:The operational heterogeneity proposed in SRC_005 abstracts the specific failure modes of 'latent shared triggers' (SRC_002) into a general principle of 'type diversity'. This abstraction is refuted if the 'Trigger-Response Divergence' (SRC_004) proves that even heterogeneous systems can be synchronized by a sufficiently global environmental shock (e.g., a leap second affecting all kernels regardless of version).
